prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
A crisper drawer may look like a simple box in the refrigerator. But its small slider can change how fresh food is kept.

Many refrigerators offer two choices: low humidity and high humidity. The low-humidity setting lets more air move through the drawer. The high-humidity setting is more closed, so it helps keep moisture inside.

Why does that matter?

Fresh produce can have two different problems. Some foods lose water quickly and become soft or wilted. Others release a natural gas as they ripen. This gas, called ethylene, can affect nearby fruits and vegetables. They may ripen too quickly and spoil sooner.

A low-humidity drawer can help the gas move away. A high-humidity drawer can help food keep its moisture.

So the best choice is not simply, “Is this a fruit or a vegetable?” The better question is, “What is most likely to go wrong with this food?”

【Point One】
Think about the food’s main risk. If early ripening from ethylene gas is the problem, choose the more open, low-humidity setting. This lets the gas escape. If water loss and wilting are the problem, choose the more closed, high-humidity setting. This can be easier than memorizing a long food list.

【Point Two】
Fruit is not always a low-humidity choice. Strawberries and oranges prefer high humidity. Tomatoes and bananas are recommended for counter storage, not the crisper. Potatoes, sweet potatoes, onions, and garlic need a cool, dry place. These examples show why one simple rule cannot fit every item.

The refrigerator drawer is small, but its job is not one-size-fits-all. It can help manage either moisture or ripening gas, depending on the food.
